components.note: The floor held where it was advertised - the 07-23 low was 10.16, just above the $10 put wall, and the $11 pin caught price into 07-17 OPEX. The stack worked; the entry was simply placed 1.60 above it.

components.claim: Options flow does not confirm the equity flow: net premium -$167k, most persistent theme is $12 Jan-28 put buying at the ask
components.note: The options tape was noise here; dark-pool/equity flow led it by roughly three weeks. FLOW-LEADS was the correct agreement call, and specifically dark-pool-leads-options.

components.claim: The upside is pre-sold: $12 call wall, triple-confirmed $13 gamma wall with covered-call writing; long-gamma dampens the squeeze inside the $11-$13 box
components.note: Price sliced both walls and closed 15.05 on 08-07, +15.8% above the $13 gamma wall. Long gamma did not cap the move once the catalyst landed - walls are resistance until a catalyst re-prices them, not a ceiling.

components.claim: No fundamental or trend endorsement: fundamentals CAUTION, insiders net sellers, consensus HOLD (UBS PT $12), price under sma200 12.95

components.note: Fired precisely as written: 12.04 (07-21) -> 10.16 (07-23), -15.6%, no support until the $10 wall. The plan named this air pocket and then placed the stock stop at 11.28, inside it.

lessons.lesson: In a name with >25% short float, express a dark-pool-shelf long as defined risk (debit spread / put credit spread), not as a stopped stock long. High-SI names resolve by violent two-way flushes that harvest stops before the thesis pays; a defined-risk structure has no stop to harvest and survives the round trip.

Never place a stock stop inside an air pocket you named in reasons_against. If a reason_against says 'no support between X and Y', the stop belongs below Y or the trade must be defined-risk. Cross-check every stop against the reasons_against list before publishing the plan.
lessons.applies_to: A3 level placement / A4 stop selection

lessons.lesson: When a debate steelman carries an explicit falsifiable test that has NOT yet fired, treat the debate-disconfirmed size cut as provisional, not permanent. Record the test and the restore condition in the plan, and restore the size step once the test comes back clean, rather than carrying a cut premised on an unverified bear case.

proposed_rubric_edits.change: In the debate-disconfirmation gate (lines ~137-140), add: if the bear's residual rests on a claim with an explicit falsifiable test that has not yet resolved, mark the size cut PROVISIONAL and emit a restore_condition (the test + the confirmation bar). Restore the size step when the test comes back clean instead of carrying the cut for the life of the plan.
proposed_rubric_edits.rationale: PATH 2026-07-13: the steelman ('$644M block is exit liquidity') carried two named tests - a 13D/13G/S-3/424B filing and large-tier buy_ratio < 0.45. Neither ever fired (buy_ratio 0.672 at review, no filing), yet the cut to starter 1.0% held through a +27% move. The gate cut size on a bear case that its own criteria falsified.

proposed_rubric_edits.change: Add an expression-selection step before sizing: when short interest > 25% of float OR the plan's own reasons_against name an air pocket between entry and stop, prefer a defined-risk options expression and mark any stock expression as secondary / wider-stop-only.
proposed_rubric_edits.rationale: PATH 2026-07-13: identical thesis, opposite results by vehicle. The stock plan lost 1R (stopped 07-14 on a wick, T1 traded the next session); the 12/13 Aug-21 call debit spread reached max value (+0.65 on 0.35 debit, +186%) and the 11/10 put credit spread held full credit. The vehicle, not the thesis, decided the outcome.

proposed_rubric_edits.change: Require the emitted plan to state ONE primary stop convention (close-basis or intraday) and to mark the other as secondary. When a close-basis signal stop and an intraday hard stop coexist, require an explicit precedence note and report R under the primary.
proposed_rubric_edits.rationale: PATH 2026-07-13 resolves to different outcomes by convention: intraday hard stop 11.28 -> LOSS -1.0R on 07-14; close-basis signal stop 11.60 -> T1 +1.04R on 07-15, then -2.12R on the 07-22 close. An eval should not have to guess which rule the plan meant.

proposed_rubric_edits.change: Require a post-T1 stop-management rule on any multi-target stock plan (e.g. move to breakeven, or trail by 1 ATR) rather than leaving the runner on the original stop.
proposed_rubric_edits.rationale: PATH 2026-07-13 has no trailing rule, so under the close-basis convention the runner gave back +1.04R and then lost 2.12R on the same original stop. The gap is silent in the current template.
